title: An Earthquake in the Town
text:
In March, a strong earthquake shook a small town near the coast. Many houses lost their windows, and some walls fell down. The people stayed outside until the ground stopped moving.

The next day, the government sent water, food, and blankets. Teams of volunteers helped families clean their homes. Scientists say that earthquakes are hard to predict, so people should always prepare an emergency bag.

questions.text: What happened to many houses in the town?
What did the government send the next day?
Why did the people stay outside after the earthquake?
options: They were waiting for the ground to stop moving
They wanted to see the sea

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about earthquakes?
options: They are hard to predict, so preparation is important
They always happen at the same time each year
They can be stopped by volunteers
They only affect houses near the sea

vocabulary.definition: a sudden shaking of the ground
people who help without being paid
a serious and unexpected situation that needs quick action
to say what will happen before it happens

paragraph_translations: Em março, um forte terremoto sacudiu uma pequena cidade perto da costa. Muitas casas perderam as janelas e algumas paredes caíram. As pessoas ficaram do lado de fora até o chão parar de tremer.

No dia seguinte, o governo enviou água, comida e cobertores. Equipes de voluntários ajudaram as famílias a limpar suas casas. Os cientistas dizem que os terremotos são difíceis de prever, por isso as pessoas devem sempre preparar uma mochila de emergência.
